The club became English champions for the first and only time in 1961-62, and famously won the Uefa Cup in 1981. Changes to Ipswich's ownership were made last year, with several investors coming on board , and Ashton said they were proving a driving force behind the scenes. "The investors are committed, they push hard, [and] no harder did they push on anything than they have done in the transfer window," said Ashton. "They were brutal with me on how hard they wanted me to keep the foot on the gas, and I think that related into not just the quantum of players that we brought in for both men's and women's teams, but quality, and I think both teams are bearing the fruits of that." Ipswich Town earned an immediate return to the Premier League after relegation in 2024-25 [Shutterstock] When Ipswich's men last went up to the Premier League in 2024, 10 of their 12 summer signings were British or Irish players acquired from other English sides. This time, the Blues have cast their net far wider, with Emersonn the first Brazilian to join the club, Sasa Lukic the first Serbian and Daizen Maeda their first Japanese player. "I think supporters should be really excited," Ashton added. "I still don't believe there are many, if any, clubs in the world that have had a growth period of success like we have had in the last five years, but we're not finished yet." Championship all-stars to global gamble - will Ipswich's approach work? European ambitions While many supporters will see success as securing Premier League status by means of a 17th place finish, Ashton did not shy away from sharing a vision for a return to European football for the first time since their 2002-03 Uefa Cup campaign. There is growing precedent, with the likes of Bournemouth, Brighton and Sunderland enjoying European competition this season, while clubs like Chelsea and Tottenham go without. He said: "I have one goal and that's to make this football club the best it can be. "I want it sustainably in the Premier League, I want it knocking on European football, I want it playing European football." Ashton said: "I want people to look at this football club and say actually, yeah, Sir Bobby [Robson] would have been proud of this, Sir Alf [Ramsey] would have been proud of this, because not only have they achieved success, but you know what - they've done it in a way that befits this club and its town, its county and its people." Portman Road plans Ashton said plans were being prepared to develop Portman Road and land surrounding it [Shaun Whitmore/BBC] Ashton confirmed there are plans to develop Portman Road and the area around it but said there is no set timeframe. "There's a lot of work to do," said Ashton. "There will be plans coming out over coming months for facility development, land around the stadium, how we want to take the whole Portman Road estate forward for many years to come. "There's a lot of work going on behind the scenes in regards to that and it's one to watch for the supporters." 'No time for regrets' For all of Town's successes, there have also been testing moments. Earlier this year, Ashton was forced to "unreservedly apologise" for the handling of Nigel Farage's visit to the club's Portman Road stadium. The Reform UK leader was photographed and filmed during a visit, posing with personalised shirts and pretending to sign a contract. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage visited the club's dressing room and posed for photos [Reform UK] Ashton said: "We make mistakes every single day. We don't get up every morning thinking, how are we going to make mistakes? "We get up every day trying to drive the football club forward. "There are things we would have always done differently... but there's no time for regrets. We've got to keep going and we've got to keep going quickly to drive this football club back to where it needs to be." 'Women's team destined for WSL' The goals of the men's team are clear - but Ashton said so to were its plans for the future of the women's team. He shared an unwavering belief that Ipswich Town Women, currently competing in the second tier, are on a certain path to the Women's Super League. Ipswich on 'inevitable' path to WSL - Boswell "I'm convinced of that," said Ashton. "We're building infrastructure, we're building staff, we're building quality players, we're building recruitment, we're building investment into the women's team now. "We have to build every area of this football club, both on and off the pitch, men's and women's - and I just think the future for this football club is extremely bright, but we have to build it as one. "You can't just build part of it and ignore another part, we're not going to do that." item.title: Braves predicted to sign $25M ex-Yankees high-impact arm to create elite duo with Chris Sale
item.description: Braves predicted to sign $25M ex-Yankees high-impact arm to create elite duo with Chris Sale originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves made the postseason in 2026 after completely missing out in 2025 due to injuries and other unfortunate circumstances. Now, this offseason will be crucial as they look to strengthen their starting rotation. The biggest positive is knowing that Chris Sale will be back. However, the Braves are going to have to find reliable arms to fill out the rotation behind him. “The Atlanta Braves enter another offseason trying to solve the same puzzle: how to enhance their starting rotation. In 2026, they hoped Spencer Strider, Spencer Schwellenbach and Hurston Waldrep were the cavalry needed to solve the issues. But all three dealt with injuries and can’t be counted on to pitch in 2027,” The Athletic’s Jesus Cano wrote. A potential target just became available. Former New York Yankees and San Diego Padres starter Michael King is now a free agent. “Right-handed starter Michael King has declined the player option on his contract with the Padres to become a free agent, sources told MLB.com on Thursday. The club has not confirmed the news on King, who will now become one of the top arms on the market entering his age-32 season,” MLB.com’s AJ Cassavell wrote. With this development, Atlanta is expected to make some sort of push. Sports Illustrated’s Harrison Smajovits believes the Braves should sign King. “His 2026 season will only fortify the reasoning. He did two things that no Braves starting pitcher can claim last season. He made 32 starts and clocked over 180 innings pitched. He posted a 3.21 ERA and a 1.17 WHIP despite only posting 156 strikeouts in that time. He achieved this by reducing hard contact (just 32.7%, according to Baseball Savant) and having a solid groundball rate,” Smajovits wrote. “Here is where the reality check comes in. You can scream that he’s a fit until you’re red in the face, but they actually have to sign a starting pitcher. It’s not a Michael King issue. It’s starting pitching in general.” This would be a great pickup for Atlanta, as King has established himself as a frontline starter in the league. The Braves are in major need of a reliable arm behind Sale who can provide stability in the rotation. King made $25 million with the Padres this season before declining the remainder of his contract. Atlanta will likely have to offer a significant amount of money, but adding a dependable starter like King could be worth the investment. item.title: Ballon d'Or 2026 voting breakdown: Harry Kane edges out Kylian Mbappe in incredibly tight race as full scores revealed
item.description: FBL-AWARD-BALLON D'OR-2026 - AFP Harry Kane has officially ended England's long wait for a Ballon d'Or winner, but the full voting breakdown reveals just how close the Bayern Munich striker came to missing out. The former Tottenham talisman secured the prestigious Golden Ball in London, edging out his nearest rival, Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe, in a nail-biting finish. A historic and narrow triumph Kane secured the Ballon d'Or by a razor-thin margin of just 28 points. The Bayern Munich striker claimed the coveted award for the first time on Monday, becoming the first English male player to win the prize since Michael Owen in 2001. The glitzy ceremony took place in Kane’s hometown of London, capping off a remarkable year for the Three Lions captain. The final tally highlights a fiercely competitive three-way race. Kane amassed 1,055 points, narrowly defeating Mbappe, who finished a close second with 1,027 points. Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal took third place, trailing significantly with 881 points despite a World Cup-winning campaign with Spain. A tense race to the finish line The polling process was filled with behind-the-scenes drama. France Football editor Vincent Garcia confirmed that the voting window was volatile, with the lead changing hands as the deadline approached . "I was watching the results in real time during the month of the vote," Garcia revealed. "Kylian Mbappe led the race for a long time, but Harry Kane came back into contention, and in the end, it was decided by a very, very small number of points." Following his landmark victory, Kane acknowledged the stiff competition he faced. "Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year," he said during his acceptance speech. "Congratulations to all the winners, all the nominees tonight – an impressive showing of what determination and hard work can really achieve, so well done." A year of contrasting fortunes Mbappe’s second-place finish marks his highest-ever Ballon d'Or ranking, surpassing his third-place standing in 2018. The Real Madrid forward dominated scoring charts across La Liga, the Champions League, and the World Cup, yet remains without the Golden Ball. His lack of major club silverware last season likely proved decisive in the final vote. Conversely, Kane’s transition to Germany has been a resounding success. The striker spearheaded Bayern Munich to a domestic league and cup double, cementing their dominance in the Bundesliga. Furthermore, Kane enjoyed crucial head-to-head victories over Mbappe on the biggest stages, notably defeating Real Madrid in the Champions League to reach the semi-finals, and helping England overcome France in the World Cup third-place play-off. There is always great urgency for the Cleveland Cavaliers to finally get their breakthrough and win the NBA championship after years of being in the running. Towns, of course, is known for his outside marksmanship and makes defensive rotations for the reigning Defensive Player of the Year that much more difficult. Wembanyama did not play very well during Game 1, Game 4, and Game 5 of the NBA Finals. He had to settle for difficult shots from the perimeter, and he had some troubles finishing near the basket as well as he didn’t have the strength to overpower Towns. During those three contests, all Spurs losses, Wemby shot 33.8% from the field, and a lot of that had to do with the fact that he doesn’t have a go-to scoring move. It was a catch-22 for Wembanyama. The Knicks would not allow him to set up shop near the basket, with Towns intentionally pushing him away from the hoop to make his life more difficult. Due to this, he had to catch the ball at the high post area, or even behind the three-point line. But his handle, despite being solid for a player his size, is not elite enough to the point where he can fashion clean looks for himself consistently. Just take a gander at some of the best scorers in the game today. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s handle is elite , he can get to his spots in the midrange at will, and his ability to make shots with defenders draped all over him is almost unparalleled in today’s NBA. Nikola Jokic, at his best, can just back up all the way to the rim, and destroy teams with his feathery touch. If they send double teams, he can just ping the ball to the open man. At this point, Wembanyama doesn’t quite have that go-to move in his offensive repertoire that he can resort to to get his team buckets when they need them. One possible solution is for him to bulk up, but at 7-foot-4, his center of gravity is always going to be high and players of Towns’ build are always just going to be able to make catches in the post difficult for him, so this isn’t exactly a catch-all panacea. Perhaps mastering the sky hook, which would be unstoppable at his height, or maybe even having his own version of the Dirk Nowitzki fadeaway would make him an even more unguardable superstar. Wembanyama is never going to be like Shaquille O’Neal who can overpower every defender that comes his way. Or he’s not going to be Hakeem Olajuwon, who was gifted with balletic feet. And that’s not necessarily bad. But having something in his repertoire that all but guarantees the Spurs two points would go a long way towards helping them get over the hump. Former Spurs star LaMarcus Aldridge already implored the 22-year-old Frenchman to develop his signature move, and then develop counter moves for it. It’s safe to say that Aldridge, who has 20,558 career points in the NBA by making a living off of that silky smooth turnaround jumper from midrange, knows what he’s talking about. Something to watch out for: the Spurs’ three-guard look Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Will starting Dylan Harper benefit the Spurs’ in the long run? Perhaps. Having their three guards (Harper, Castle, and De’Aaron Fox) get more and more accustomed to playing with one another should help them build the requisite chemistry to power this team to a title. But there might be some skillset incompatibility among those three that the Spurs have to watch out for. Those three appear to be at their best with the ball in their hands, and someone has to sacrifice touches whenever they all share the floor together. So far, Castle is the one who’s having to adjust the most. He is averaging a bonkers 8.2 three-point attempts per game heading into their Friday night contest against the Minnesota Timberwolves, which is up by over four attempts from his average last season. But as Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla said, many get so fixated over starting lineups when they’re just units that start games . Nonetheless, the Spurs have to be keeping a close eye on this situation, and they could always deploy a more balanced lineup by giving Julian Champagnie more minutes when the games matter the most and by utilizing Tobias Harris, who is currently still dealing with a calf strain. item.title: Injured Army veteran represents GB at golf in US
item.description: Steve Dickinson is representing Team GB for the third time [Simpson Cup] An injured Army veteran has been chosen to represent Great Britain in a golf competition against the US. The Simpson Cup is an international tournament for wounded and injured military veterans, taking place from Sunday at Shady Oaks Country Club in Texas. Steve Dickinson, 61, from Peterborough, needed a complete knee replacement for an injury he got after serving with the British Army in the first Gulf War in 1991 . He has been selected for the team for the third consecutive time and said: "Having served my country in uniform, being given the opportunity to represent Great Britain again through sport is something I am immensely proud of." The Simpson Cup has been running since 2012 and raises funds and awareness for the work of the On Course Foundation, which supports the recovery of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans through golf events and opportunities for employment in the golf industry. The Ryder Cup-style tournament "showcases the unique position of golf as one of the few sports where players of all skills and abilities can play together on a level playing field, because of the official golf handicap system", the foundation said. Dickinson plays at Peterborough Milton Golf Club and his handicap is 11.7. He served with the Army Catering Corps between 1981 and 1995. Team GB currently leads the US by seven wins to six in the annual competition. Steve Dickinson celebrated with team members after their last win [Simpson Cup] Speaking about the work of the foundation, Dickinson said: "It helps us get back into civilian life, and the camaraderie, the friendship - it's just about us getting together. "My injury is nothing compared to these guys - some of them are limbless, mine was just playing football in the Army in Cyprus after the Gulf War. "I got injured and five years ago I had a full knee replacement and that's still ongoing and I need it replacing again. So it's never ending — the injury's always there." BBC Sport: Golf The foundation helps with any injury, he said. "It can be physical, it can be mental, but it helps everybody get together... it's such a great, great atmosphere." The tournaments are "full-on banter" with the opponents, "from the minute we get there to the minute we leave", Dickinson said. "We all take the mickey out of each other," he added. "But when we play the Americans, it's a serious competition to be fair; we are serious on the day." Do you have a story suggestion for Peterborough? Contact us below. [hands together/praying emoji],” Mixon posted on X on October 30. It’s all in God hands, never lose faith.🙏 — ⚡️Primetime!!!⚡️ (@Joe_MainMixon) October 31, 2026 Mixon shared a video teasing his new athletic sock line, but also teasing his comeback. The Seahawks bit, bringing him in for a visit and eleven making plans to sign the former 48th overall pick of the 2017 draft. However, the Seahawks had a change of heart after getting Mixon in for a look. “As it turns out, the Seahawks decided not to sign veteran running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after he underwent a physical for the team, per league source,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported in a post on Threads on October 6, adding that “Mixon will remain a free agent.” Ex-Bengals, Texans RB Joe Mixon’s Football Future in Jeopardy Mixon’s foot injury has remained shrouded in mystery. He was spotted in a walking boot last offseason and is believed to have undergone a surgical procedure. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald did not provide any more clarity about the decision. “Just didn’t work out. Didn’t work out,” Macdonald told reporters on October 7. “Probably the most we should say about it with respect to the process. But those things happen, and it’s just part of the process.” Mixon, 30, has rushed for 7,428 yards and 60 touchdowns on 1,816 carries. He has another 2,448 yards and 14 TDs on 319 receptions. As it stands, his football future appears grim. “I don’t think this is some sort of mystery some are making it out to be,” Alexander posted on X on October 6, “He did NOT shoot himself. He has a rare medical condition he’s choosing to make private. He worked w/ doctors to help heal his foot. “The only surprise for me, is that it was never leaked to a national insider, which was likely per the request of his agent and Mixon.” Alexander called the Texans the “NFL’s most tight-lipped team” and said they “happily obliged.” Y’all just don’t know, what I been through this passed year & a half… Just know that’s all God🙏🥺 He will test your faith, keep trusting, stay patient, and believe in His timing. Never lose hope or give up. Your breakthrough is coming. 💯 — ⚡️Primetime!!!⚡️ (@Joe_MainMixon) October 5, 2026 Texans general manager Nick Caserio downplayed the idea of the injury being the result of Mixon acting irresponsibly. Head coach DeMeco Ryans opted to respect Mixon’s privacy during the ordeal. “It’s also possible those national reporters probably saw no benefit to leaking it,” Alexander said, highlighting how much uncertainty still remains around the situation. At one point, Mixon pushed back on the idea that he would miss the season. NFL Insider Right About Joe Mixon NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported the expectation that Mixon would miss the season on X in November 2025 “as he deals with a foot injury from the offseason,” adding that he “likely remains on the Physically Unable to Perform list through the season.” To that, Mixon said , “Now, I get everyone’s looking for splash news & clickbait… but I’m just curious, Ian how do you know more about me than me? [confused face emoji].” As it turned out, though, Rapoport was right. Mixon did not play at all in 2025. Caserio noted a pattern of progress and setbacks that essentially left them stuck in neutral. In the end, the Texans moved on from Mixon. The Seahawks decided the former Bengals star is still not healthy enough to contribute. item.title: Warriors predicted to trade for Thunder's 7-foot-1 NBA champion to replace Kristaps Porzingis
item.description: Warriors predicted to trade for Thunder's 7-foot-1 NBA champion to replace Kristaps Porzingis originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . For the Golden State Warriors , it has been an okay start to the season, but the most frustrating part of the offseason came from their inability to sign any big-name players. One of the players Golden State did sign was veteran Kristaps Porzingis. The seven-footer is known for his size, but also for his history of missing significant time due to injuries. Porzingis has not been around the team since training camp began. “That has meant an out-of-sight, out-of-mind strategy when it comes to the ongoing absence of presumed starting center Kristaps Porzingis, who was re-signed this summer despite missing 90 games over the past two seasons with three different teams. Ever since Porzingis called out of work one day prior to training camp, the front office instructed Steve Kerr to strategize and prep his team as if Porzingis was a nonfactor,” ESPN’s Anthony Slater wrote. With it being highly unlikely that Porzingis plays this season, or perhaps ever again, the Warriors are trying to find a trade partner. “Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome), sources tell ESPN," ESPN's Shams Charania posted. Through the first week of the season, it has become clear that Golden State is undersized. Bleacher Report’s Dan Favale believes the Warriors could trade for Oklahoma City Thunder center Chet Holmgren. “Perhaps Aday Mara is so good so fast that the Oklahoma City Thunder end up rethinking their monster commitment to Chet Holmgren amid an expected belly flop into second-apron territory next season,” Favale wrote. Holmgren would be a great replacement for Porzingis, as he is younger and the Warriors would have control over him for the next few seasons. Holmgren also already has championship experience. Holmgren is currently on a $239 million contract with the Thunder. The Warriors are in major need of size, and acquiring Holmgren would be a significant addition. It would also benefit Steph Curry tremendously. All of this would need to happen when he recovers from his injury of course. item.title: Lakers fans clown Yaxel Lendeborg after dominant Luka Doncic performance
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Lakers fans clown Yaxel Lendeborg after dominant Luka Doncic performance appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The ongoing feud between Luka Doncic and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has increasingly resembled a dramatic rivalry. On Friday, Lendeborg had the last laugh as the Golden State Warriors secured a 112-95 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers . However, the rookie struggled to make an impact against Doncic’s outstanding performance, which quickly made him a target of criticism and trolling from Lakers fans. Lendeborg made a statement before the game by arriving at the arena dressed in a Michael Myers costume. Such a bold entrance naturally raised expectations for his performance on the court. However, Doncic stole the spotlight with his dominant display, leaving the Warriors rookie facing plenty of online mockery. “ Yaxel Lendeborg did all that to show up and drop 6 points,” one fan mocked . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Yaxel 6’9 for nothing dude plays trash against the Lakers but good against everybody else,” a fan remarked . “ Yaxel Lendeborg is currently a -22 while his team is winning by 12 points and Luka Doncic is a +11 while being down 12 points,” one user added . “NBA hypes up the Luka and Yaxel Lendeborg beef only for Yaxel to have zero shot attempts all game,” another comment read . The Lakers superstar finished with 37 points, seven rebounds and five assists in 37 minutes. He shot 12-of-27 from the field, including 6-of-16 from beyond the arc, and converted seven of his eight free-throw attempts. Doncic also recorded one steal and two blocks. Meanwhile, Lendeborg finished with six points and one rebound in 24 minutes for the Warriors. However, he did not record an assist and finished with five turnovers and six personal fouls. Despite Lendeborg’s modest contribution, the Warriors managed to come away with the victory behind another impressive performance from Stephen Curry. Golden State found itself trailing Los Angeles by as many as 25 points early in the second quarter, but the team gradually turned things around and eventually secured a 17-point win. The loss dropped the Lakers to a 4-2 record for the season, while Golden State improved to 3-3. item.title: “How Many All-Pros Does Tom Brady Have?”: Rob Parker Makes Massive Claim About Lamar Jackson’s NFL Legacy By Comparing Him To 7x SB Winner
item.description: Lamar Jackson © Imagn NFL analyst Rob Parker showered praise on Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson and compared him to seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady. On The Odd Couple Show, Parker highlighted Jackson’s three First-Team All-Pro selections and compared them with Brady, who earned the same number in 23 seasons. “The best quarterback in the NFL is Lamar Jackson,” Parker said. “How many All-Pros does Tom Brady have? Tom Brady had three All-Pros. Three in 23. Lamar has three already in two-thirds less time. He already has three.” Brady also had three Second-Team All-Pro selections. The former Patriots quarterback won three MVP awards, while Jackson has won two. Parker added that Jackson was robbed of the MVP award in 2024 and claimed he had a better season than eventual winner, Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen. “He should have three MVPs,” Parker continued. “The best year he had in the National Football League didn’t give him the MVP. They gave him first-team All-Pro, but they gave Josh Allen the MVP because they felt sorry for him. It went against everything we know in the National Football League. It was terrible.” In that season, Jackson threw for 4,172 yards, 41 touchdowns and four interceptions. Meanwhile, Allen threw for 3,731 yards, 28 touchdowns, and six interceptions. In the voting , Allen received 383 points and 27 first-place votes, while Jackson finished with 362 points and 23 first-place votes. Rob Parker Excuses Lamar Jackson Of Super Bowl-Less Career While Lamar Jackson is considered one of the best quarterbacks in the league, his lack of postseason success takes some of the shine off his career. Tom Brady made 10 Super Bowl appearances and won seven championships. On the other hand, Jackson has zero Super Bowl appearances in eight seasons. However, according to Rob Parker, the Ravens quarterback has been let down by his teammates. “Zay Flowers, a fumble. Mark Andrews can’t catch a two-point conversion to tie the game in Buffalo. It’s happened over and over again,” Parker said. “Last year, to get into the playoffs and to win the division, guess what happened? Lamar drove the team down the field in Pittsburgh, and the kicker missed a field goal.” Jackson has missed three straight games due to a high ankle sprain sustained in Week 4, but is expected to return when the Ravens face the Bills on Sunday. item.title: WWE succession plan emerges as Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles eye new roles
item.description: Photo by MICHAEL TRAN/AFP via Getty Images WWE Hall of Famers Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles are reportedly in line for major backstage promotions as the company prepares for a significant change in its creative leadership. Bruce Prichard, WWE’s Executive Director of Creative Writing and Talent, is expected to retire after WrestleMania 43, although he could remain involved with the company as a consultant. Michaels is reportedly being lined up to replace Prichard in 2027, while Styles could take on a more hands-on role with WWE’s developmental brand, NXT. Shawn Michaels could replace Bruce Prichard as AJ Styles takes on NXT role According to reports from PWInsider , Michaels is expected to move into Prichard’s position, with preparations for the transition already expected to begin in the coming months. The former WWE champion has led NXT since 2021, when Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque underwent a cardiac procedure. Michaels was subsequently promoted to Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative. His experience with developing young wrestlers makes him a natural candidate for a more prominent position within WWE’s creative structure. Michaels also shares a longstanding friendship with Triple H, which could prove valuable as the pair continue shaping the company’s future. However, his potential promotion would leave a significant opening at NXT, with AJ Styles reportedly emerging as a candidate to take on greater responsibilities. According to False Finish, WWE officials expect Styles to become more involved with the developmental brand following Michaels’ departure from the role. Styles has previously expressed a desire to help prepare the next generation of WWE superstars, particularly after stepping away from in-ring competition. Triple H discussed the former champion’s plans during an appearance on Cody Rhodes’ podcast, explaining that Styles had explored several backstage positions before identifying the area that suited him best. “He really likes is getting to these young kids, spotting talent, and trying to help fan the flames of that little spark and turn it into something more, the developmental side,” Triple H said. Styles’ interest in mentoring young wrestlers could make him a strong fit for NXT, where emerging talent is prepared for the main roster. The Phenomenal One brings plenty of experience to the role, having won both WWE and TNA World Championships and becoming one of just 22 Grand Slam champions in WWE history. Styles was also inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame during WrestleMania 42 week. With Prichard’s expected retirement approaching, WWE could soon have two familiar names taking on new responsibilities behind the scenes. item.title: Mike Brown calls out the Knicks' mediocre defense in the loss against the 76ers
item.description: Mike Brown calls out the Knicks' mediocre defense in the loss against the 76ers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In the New York Knicks ' first game in their NBA Cup defense, they unfortunately lost the game 98-93 to the Philadelphia 76ers . It was a superb performance by the 76ers ' Tyrese Maxey, but it seems they really capitalized on the Knicks ' defense. New York head coach Mike Brown was frustrated about how the Knicks looked on defense. It was a frustrating night because it was a big blow to the hopes of an NBA Cup repeat and another loss that drops them to a 2-4 record. Mike Brown laments the Knicks' troubling defense against the 76ers It is a challenging result for the Knicks because the Knicks had the chance to get back on track to a 3-3 record. Unfortunately, they suffered yet another loss to the 76ers, which gives them a 2-0 edge in the head-to-head matchup. While Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns scored over 20 points apiece, it was still quite an underwhelming performance for the Knicks. This is not what people would like to see, especially with their status as defending champions. MORE: Mike Brown's reality check from the slow start to the Knicks' season Scoring 93 points is not the optimal approach to a game but it seems that Brown had more of a problem with what transpired on defense. He was not a fan of how easy the 76ers had it at certain points in the game. "Gotta give Philadelphia credit; they won the ball game. When you watch this game, though, especially in the first half, how they got downhill so easily. They were getting in our paint left and right. It was really, really easy; we weren't in our shifts," Brown said about the Knicks' defense after the game . "To continue to have that ball dribbling into the paint, especially in the paint when they shot 5-7 from the three-point line, was not good." Brown also commented about how the Knicks are trying to hit home runs on every offensive play. It is definitely an inconsistent approach to the game across both sides of the ball, and Brown wants to fix that moving forward if they want any chances of getting back to the top of the Eastern Conference standings. item.title: Teen football photographer 'living the dream'
item.description: Tiego Greno has progressed from photographing lower league matches to Premier League games [Tiego Greno] From taking photos of grassroots football matches up to Champions League games - all by the age of 18 - Tiego Greno says he is "living the dream". The teenager from Chelmsford started taking photos of lower league football in 2023, before becoming Chelmsford City's club photographer for the 2025-26 season. Now he has started taking photos of Premier League and European matches, including Arsenal's recent away fixture against Bayern Munich. "I just want to be everywhere, every single day if it's possible," he told the BBC. Greno started work with a photography agency aged 17 which was something he says came with challenges, given his age. "Many of these stadiums don't allow anyone under 18 to work in those environments, so I had to be restricted," he told BBC Essex's James Patient. Still only 18, Greno's photography has taken him to stadiums including Real Madrid's Bernabeu [Tiego Greno] But his work began to speak for itself. Just three days after his 18th birthday, he won the sports category at the East Anglian Photography Awards, with his photo of Southend United players crestfallen as their opponents Oldham Athletic celebrated promotion back to the Football League at Wembley Stadium in June 2025. "I think that picture really summarised what can happen in the sport - you could be winning for the entire game and then in the last minute it all turns around," he said. Greno says he is grateful to his family for being able to afford his camera equipment, especially his father and fellow photographer Antonio. "Without him, probably I wouldn't be where I am right now," he said. Antonio said it was "impossible not to be proud" of his son. "For me, this journey has been… more than photography, it's been about watching my son discovering what he loves and, most importantly, having the courage to follow," he told the BBC. His son said: "I'm already living the dream. It's just keeping it really consistent and if I can do it every day, perfect." Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below. item.title: 'Showed me a lot': Skip Bayless reacts to what Luka Doncic did after Steph Curry 'broke his ankles'
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Stephen Curry and Luka Doncic, unsurprisingly, have made the headlines following the Golden State Warriors’ 112-95 win over the Los Angeles Lakers in the NBA Cup. The Lakers started the game in tremendous fashion, leading the first quarter 38-15. At one point in the game, they were even 25 points ahead, but they ended up losing by 17 in the end. The most eye-catching moment, though, was when Curry embarrassed Doncic before scoring a three-pointer. Skip Bayless praises Luka Doncic’s reaction after Steph Curry dropped him Both Doncic and Curry are among the best players in the NBA, so seeing them go up against each other is always a treat. On Friday night, after a stunning first-quarter performance by the Slovenian, Curry turned up and helped his side win the game. At one moment, when Doncic and Curry came face to face, ‘the latter’s dribbling skills caused the Lakers star to lose his balance and fall down. Curry then calmly converted a three-pointer, making that a very memorable moment. We’re sure it will be played back over and over again. Despite that, Doncic showed immense class after the game and shook hands with all the Warriors players. That caught Skip Bayless’ eye. He tweeted: “Luka showed me a lot by congratulating the Warriors stars, especially Steph, who “broke his ankles.”” That really was great to see, and it showed what kind of a man Doncic is. He could easily have walked back into the locker room, but staying back to congratulate the opponents after a defeat and an embarrassing moment is a classy move. item.title: Pistons predicted to trade for $179M ex-Nuggets sharpshooting NBA champion to address weakness
item.description: Pistons predicted to trade for $179M ex-Nuggets sharpshooting NBA champion to address weakness originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Pistons were the best team in the Eastern Conference during the regular season last year, but they quickly realized they were still an inexperienced group when it came to the playoffs. This season, they are hungry to get back and prove they can take the next step. However, the organization explored several different ways to bring star players to the Motor City. They were prepared to offer Austin Reaves a contract and also made calls about Kevin Durant and Kawhi Leonard. “The Pistons inquired about trading for Kawhi Leonard and Kevin Durant this offseason, according to league sources, and were positioned to offer Austin Reaves a big free agent contract if the Los Angeles Lakers opened the door. None of that materialized," ESPN's Vincent Goodwill wrote. One of the biggest weaknesses from last season that could continue to hold Detroit back is its ability to shoot from beyond the three-point line. “Most notably, the Pistons are even snagging wins when they shoot poorly from beyond the arc. In an era of basketball where consistency from three-point range is preached as paramount, the Detroit Pistons are winning in their own way. Their tough defense and efficiency inside the paint has defined their identity this season," SI's Aidan Chacon wrote. Adding a shooter will undoubtedly be one of the Pistons' priorities ahead of the trade deadline. CBS Sports' Sam Quinn believes they should pursue a trade for NBA champion Michael Porter Jr. “Get ready to hear a lot about the Detroit Pistons today, folks. A team that needs offense and controls all of its own picks is always going to feature prominently in deadline speculation, and Porter is the first of many candidates who will come up for them here,” Quinn wrote. Porter would be a great addition because he offers exactly what the team needs as a shooter while also bringing NBA Finals experience. He could become an important presence in Detroit's locker room as well. Porter is currently playing on a $179 million contract with the Brooklyn Nets and is coming off a strong campaign last season. If the Pistons want to add a proven scorer, Porter would certainly be a good option. item.title: Tottenham receive MASSIVE James Maddison injury boost ahead of Crystal Palace clash
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Coventry City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham Hotspur have received a significant boost with manager Roberto De Zerbi confirming James Maddison is available to face Crystal Palace on Saturday. The England international suffered an injury scare against Chelsea, but he is now in contention to feature alongside the returning Destiny Udogie. Maddison shakes off injury scare Maddison has been cleared to play against Palace in the Premier League this Saturday. The England international sparked injury fears after being substituted early in the second half of a 2-0 victory at Chelsea . However, manager De Zerbi confirmed the playmaker has avoided a serious setback. Maddison will now be part of the matchday squad for the weekend fixture. De Zerbi confirms special player is available Maddison followed a modified training programme this week to manage his workload following the early substitution. Despite missing a couple of full sessions, De Zerbi insists the midfielder is ready to contribute. "This week he didn't work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us," De Zerbi told a press conference on Friday. The Tottenham boss must now decide whether to start the midfielder or utilise him from the bench against Palace. The coaching staff will evaluate his final fitness levels before kick-off. Managing a careful return to fitness Fitness remains a sensitive topic for Maddison after a difficult period on the sidelines. He missed the majority of last season with an ACL injury and suffered a shoulder problem during an opening-weekend defeat at Brentford. He recently marked his return to the starting XI by opening the scoring against Coventry City earlier this month. The club is now taking a cautious approach to ensure he stays fit for the remainder of the campaign. "For Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks," De Zerbi added. "So, I think it's not a problem if he loses two days, but then we have to analyse if we take the risk or not." Udogie returns to bolster the squad Maddison is not the only player returning to action for Tottenham this weekend. Full-back Udogie is also set to feature after missing the last two games with a knee injury. The dual return of Maddison and Udogie provides a massive lift for the team. item.title: “It’s The Kobe Bryant Thing” – MLB Insider Reveals Behind-The-Scenes of Shohei Ohtani’s Controversial Decision During NLCS
item.description: Shohei Ohtani - LA Dodgers | © Imagn MLB insider Jim Bowden shared details about the Los Angeles Dodgers’ decision to keep Shohei Ohtani in the lineup despite fitness concerns during the 2026 National League Championship Series. Ohtani’s availability became a major talking point during the series against the Milwaukee Brewers. With the Dodgers trailing 0-3 and the Japanese superstar struggling at the plate, manager Dave Roberts, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, and general manager Brandon Gomes reportedly met with him ahead of Game 4. The Dodgers were concerned about Ohtani’s left knee irritation and right biceps tightness. The management considered removing him from the starting lineup to protect his health and give the offense a different look. However, Ohtani reportedly insisted on playing and refused to be benched for Game 4. While sharing these meeting details ahead of Game 4 on ‘97.1 The Fan LA,’ Bowden also said the Dodgers ultimately chose to trust their superstar rather than overrule his decision. “What the Dodgers chose to do was, I’m going to trust my superstar. He says he’s fine. And by the way, he homered in game four, right? So, I mean, we can’t really second guess that final decision when he sits there and homers that next game, right? But I think it’s the Kobe Bryant thing, right? Like with the Lakers, what would happen if Kobe went in and said, “I’m playing.” Kobe would have played, right? I know it’s a little different in the NBA. I get it. But I think what Dave Roberts and Andrew Friedman were doing was trusting their superstar. And I think we all understand that. And so they decided they were going to go with him.” However, Ohtani’s home run was not enough to prevent the Dodgers from being swept by Milwaukee. He hit a three-run homer in the second inning of Game 4 but struck out in his other three at-bats, including a crucial late-game appearance with the tying run at third base. He finished the 2026 postseason with a .192 batting average and 10 strikeouts. What did Shohei Ohtani say after the Dodgers’ postseason exit? After the Dodgers’ 6-4 defeat to the Brewers on October 15, Shohei Ohtani spoke to reporters in a post-game interview about the team’s elimination. He praised Milwaukee’s performance and acknowledged that the opponents had exposed weaknesses in his game. “The Brewers were overall strong, and a very good team. And [they] really exposed parts of me as a player, and got to give some credit to that,” said Shohei Ohtani. Shohei Ohtani’s injury concerns had also affected his availability during the regular season. He dealt with left knee inflammation in June and later missed time in September with right biceps inflammation. He finished the 2026 regular season with 523 at-bats, 89 runs, and 144 hits across 135 games. item.title: Emiliano Martinez reveals finger injury 'will NEVER return' to normal as Chelsea star admits to 'zombie' World Cup struggle with Argentina
item.description: Chelsea FC v Brighton & Hove Albion - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Emiliano Martinez has opened up on the harrowing physical toll of his career, admitting that a significant finger injury sustained earlier this year will never truly heal. The Chelsea goalkeeper revealed he was forced to play through extreme pain to help Argentina, leaving him with permanent damage that still affects his game today. Playing through the pain for Argentina Martinez suffered a broken and dislocated finger in May during the warm-up for Aston Villa's Europa League final victory against Freiburg. The severe injury immediately cast doubt over his involvement in Argentina's World Cup title defence, leaving the 34-year-old devastated when he first saw the scans. Rather than undergoing surgery that would have ruled him out of the tournament, Martinez chose to play through the agony. Backed by Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni, the shot-stopper relied on a customised Adidas glove for protection, despite admitting the heavy strapping severely restricted his ability to grasp the ball. 'Every single night I was crying' Speaking to Argentine journalist Gaston Edul’s YouTube channel, the veteran goalkeeper detailed the severe physical and emotional toll the injury took on his daily life. The pain was so intense that it completely altered his training methods and required immense personal sacrifice. "The day before Algeria I was diving with one arm, diving like a zombie," Martinez explained. "If I put my hand down I was seeing stars. It was brutal. Every single night I was crying because my finger looked like a sausage." Despite the permanent consequences, the Argentine insists he has no regrets about putting his country first. "It will never go back to how it was," he said. "I am still playing with pain. But these are the risks you take for the national team, I’d do it again." A collapsed transfer to Juventus The finger problem had significant ramifications for Martinez's club career during the summer window. A prospective move to Serie A giants Juventus ultimately broke down once the full extent of the damage was discovered during his medical assessments. "I got an x-ray and it was broken again," the goalkeeper revealed. "That is when a transfer to a club fell through because of the finger." Their extraordinary accuracy has raised serious questions about a potential leak of confidential results before football’s most prestigious individual award. Harry Kane was crowned the winner at the ceremony at the London Palladium, finishing ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Lionel Messi. item.title: Grealish could have been Everton’s poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limbo
item.description: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man. That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. Six Everton appearances into this campaign he was left out of the squad for Thursday’s Carabao Cup win against Newcastle after missing training on Monday. Everton went public with the fact that there had been “ a breach of club discipline ”. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
